messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging on-call (priority=high) — streaming gateway 5xx spike + client cancels observed. Root metrics: gateway 5xx +110% in last 3m, stream disconnects up ~3x. https://metrics.internal/r/streaming (auto-report)

sara (SRE): seeing lots of chunked EOFs on gateway nodes, logs show repeated "http2: stream closed" and backend 502s. Started correlation by route /v1/chat/stream.

raj (oncall): I'm on it, joining in. brief please: customer-visible impact? any billing spikes?

alyssa (support): early reports from 4 customers (two marketplaces) seeing partial responses then client reconnects. No billing anomalies yet, but user-facing timeouts. Severity: P1 for impacted customers.

miguel (runtime): stacktrace snippets from runtime: ```2026-03-15T14:32:18Z runtime: kv cache miss, slot 204; error: write tcp 10.1.3.22:443->10.2.5.8:51234: write: connection reset by peer``` Also seeing high mem mgmt GC stalls on a subset of pods.

kevin (prod-eng): rolling canary deployed 02:12 UTC changed socket keepalive semantics. Could be related. Can we rollback canary to verify?

raj (oncall): good catch. miguel can you patch a quick revert on canary nodes? If rollback takes >5m fallback to routing policy to avoid canary.

miguel (runtime): reverting canary now — command: ```kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/gateway-canary --to-revision=12``` Tail logs to watch.

incident-bot: Automated action: muted noisy alerts for gateway-hosted-5xx for 2m to reduce fatigue.

sara (SRE): While revert runs, propose two live mitigations: 1) Route new streaming requests to fallback cluster (older runtime) 2) Temporarily reduce per-connection max tokens to limit long-lived streams. Which should we do first?

kevin (prod-eng): Do fallback routing first (less intrusive). How fast to flip?

raj (oncall): Flip now. rctl command: ```rctl route set-policy streaming fallback-cluster=true --scope=global``` Applying. Watch for CPU spike on fallback nodes.

miguel (runtime): applied fallback route. Telemetry shows inbound traffic to fallback rising. 5xx rate dropping from 12%->4% on gateway within 45s.

alyssa (support): customers reporting fewer disconnects after ~2 minutes. Sending quick update to affected customers: "We identified a routing issue and have routed traffic to a more stable cluster; continuing to monitor."

customer-ops: please capture list of impacted request_ids and users for postmortem. Alyssa, I can pull logs once we mark the time window.

sara (SRE): still seeing chunked encoding partial frames for some legacy clients — looks like client-cancel spike at 14:33:20. Metrics: client_cancel_count +350% on route sig-chat-long. Possible client SDK bug triggered by repeated partial frames.

raj (oncall): roll-forward mitigations: 1) enable short-lived heartbeat frames for streaming to keep client connections alive 2) increase reconnect jitter on gateway to avoid fanout surge. Which is lower risk?

miguel (runtime): heartbeat is quick: ```feature-toggle set streaming-heartbeat true --ttl=1h``` Doing that now. Also will reduce max-fanout per-user from 8->4 to blunt cascade.

incident-bot: action logged by raj.heartbeat_toggle by miguel.

kevin (prod-eng): observed a tight window where many clients retried aggressively and caused conn churn. We should add client-visible guidance (SDK) to backoff randomized by up to 10s. Alyssa, can you get a note into support channels?

alyssa (support): drafting a short SDK advisory: "If you see partial responses, please upgrade to SDK v2.4.1 which includes jittered backoff. Workaround: increase client read timeout to 90s." Will post in customers channel in 5m.

sara (SRE): rollback complete — canary undo to revision 12 finished at 14:35:03. Reverted nodes show lower GC and fewer connection resets.

miguel (runtime): GC tuning param revert also applied. Runtime heap pressure dropping. 5xx now ~1.5% over baseline. Streaming disconnects down by ~70% vs peak.

raj (oncall): summary of live mitigations performed: - Reverted canary rollout - Routed streaming traffic to fallback cluster - Enabled streaming heartbeat - Reduced per-user fanout - Muted noisy alerts - Posted SDK advisory to customers

sara (SRE): open items: - Postmortem: collect timeline + root cause (canary change + GC interplay) - Long-term: add automated canary rollback on connection-error spike - Observe for 2 hours before closing.

kevin (prod-eng): agreed. I'll own the canary policy change to include a 3-minute gated health check on connection errors. Ticket: RDW-INC-2026 (will create after this thread).

alyssa (support): customer update sent. Affected customers: 4 (IDs captured). No data loss reported. Customers asked for ETA on full stability — tell them 2h monitoring, next update in 30m.

customer-ops: pulling logs for impacted request_ids now: query: ```/logs?q=route:streaming AND ts:["2026-03-15T14:30:00" TO "2026-03-15T14:37:00"] AND (error:502 OR error:reset)``` Will attach in postmortem doc.

raj (oncall): handoff plan: I'll stay on for 30m, then pass to sara. If metrics degrade (5xx>5% sustained or client_cancel spike), page pager escalation.

sara (SRE): acknowledged. tagging this thread with PMs and security for awareness. Will start the incident doc: https://incidents.internal/3487654321 (placeholder)

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=high, phase=mitigated->monitoring, owner=raj.

kevin (prod-eng): small follow-up: add canary test to CI that simulates partial chunked frames (we don't cover that path). I'll open a PR.

raj (oncall): last check: 14:36:38 gateway 5xx stable ~1.2%, client_cancel back near baseline. Closing active mitigation; moving to monitoring. Last update in 30m.

alyssa (support): leaving final customer note: "We've routed traffic to a stable cluster and applied mitigations. We'll continue monitoring and will follow up in 2 hours with the root cause and next steps." :white_check_mark:

sara (SRE): thanks all. Postmortem owners: kevin (prod-eng) + sara (SRE) + alyssa (support). Please add timeline entries to RDW-INC-2026 doc.

miguel (runtime): adding final logs dump to incident doc now.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation at 14:36:38; monitoring window open until 16:36:38.
